title: Brain, head and neck and spine anatomy

steps.tx: The intracranial arterial collateral network exhibits frequent developmental hypoplasia or agenesis. A completely formed **Circle of Willis** polygon is present in only 20% to 30% of normal individuals, consisting of the paired internal carotid arteries, paired A1 segments, the single **anterior communicating artery**, paired posterior communicating arteries, and paired P1 segments.

steps.tx: The paired dural venous sinuses flanking the sella turcica demonstrate crucial neurovascular relationships. Traversing freely within the central venous lumen of the **cavernous sinus** are the internal carotid artery and **abducens nerve** (CN VI), whereas cranial nerves III, IV, V1, and V2 are embedded within its fibrous lateral dural wall.
steps.say: The paired dural venous sinuses flanking the sella turcica demonstrate crucial neurovascular relationships. Traversing freely within the central venous lumen of the cavernous sinus are the internal carotid artery and abducens nerve, whereas cranial nerves 3, 4, V1, and V2 are embedded within its fibrous lateral dural wall.

steps.tx: The meatal fundus is separated by distinct osteofibrous crests that establish four cranial nerve quadrants. Within the **internal auditory canal**, the transverse falciform crest and vertical **Bill bar** organise the nerves: the facial nerve (CN 7) traverses anterosuperiorly ('seven up'), the cochlear nerve traverses anteroinferiorly, and vestibular nerves lie posteriorly.

steps.tx: The cranial base outlet transmitting posterior cranial nerves and venous outflow is anatomically compartmentalised. The **jugular foramen** divides into the smaller anteromedial **pars nervosa**, transmitting glossopharyngeal CN 9 and inferior petrosal sinus, and the larger posterolateral pars vascularis transmitting vagus CN 10, accessory CN 11, and internal jugular vein.

steps.tx: Standardised cranial nerve pathways must be recognised on skull base cross-sectional imaging. The maxillary nerve courses through the **foramen rotundum** to the pterygopalatine fossa, the mandibular nerve traverses the **foramen ovale** to the masticator space, while hypoglossal CN 12 traverses the hypoglossal canal to the tongue.

steps.tx: Deep facial architecture is organized by the three layers of the deep fascia. Enclosed by the superficial layer of the **deep cervical fascia**, the **masticator space** houses the muscles of mastication, the ascending ramus and body of the mandible, and the mandibular nerve (V3).

steps.tx: The retrovisceral midline potential space provides a direct conduit for descending mediastinal sepsis. The **retropharyngeal space** extends from the skull base down to the superior mediastinum (T3 to T6 vertebral level), bounded posteriorly by the **alar fascia** and communicating with the dangerous space.

left.title: Retropharyngeal Space
points: Extends from skull base to T3-T6
Contains fat and retropharyngeal lymph nodes

right.title: Danger Space
points: Extends from skull base to diaphragm

steps.tx: Spinal cord terminations determine safe anatomical interventional boundaries. The adult spinal cord **conus medullaris** normally terminates at the L1-L2 intervertebral disc space, with a low-lying conus terminating below L2 indicating spinal dysraphism and a **tethered spinal cord** in radiological evaluations.
